items.reason: The accepted Source Identity Maintenance behavior is implemented and QA-accepted, but the distinct Intent remains structurally unmapped because its approved architecture deliberately extends the already-confirmed MappingEngine and supporting adapters instead of introducing a unique source component. Assigning a second canonical Intent GUID to that same class would invent a source identity and violate the one-confirmed-identity model. This is source-traceability representation drift requiring a later architecture decision, not missing implementation and not authorization for more product code.

items.statement: A read-only review can explicitly select one current observed Reality class or function even when name matching produces no candidate, then bind its exact source location, source hash, observed GUID, intent evidence, and deterministic digest for human review.
A read-only refresh review can bind one already marker-confirmed symbol and its current adjacent receipt to fresh deterministic evidence without changing source or canonical state.

An explicitly approved candidate mapping or receipt refresh applies atomically only when the reviewed digest, marker, symbol, path, source content, and canonical DAGs remain fresh; every mismatch or failure leaves source, receipts, DAGs, backlog, and audit state unchanged or fully restored.

Python API, CLI, MCP, and Codex workflow guidance expose the same bounded, human-readable decision contract, keep GUIDs and digests in the audit section, and never treat mapping approval as behavioral approval.

Adversarial path, symlink, reparse-point, hardlink, duplicate-marker, stale-writer, and concurrent-review cases fail closed, while a fresh self-dogfood run can review the MCP v2 representative symbol and both stale confirmed receipts without manual marker or receipt edits.
